samples.summary: `verify-frame.mjs` still builds only the shell, so it hits exactly the `Cannot find module …/dist/plugin/index.js` / stale-plugin trap this PR fixes in its three sibling scripts
samples.evidence: This PR updated `verify-consumer.mjs` (same package), `verify-scenes.mjs` and `verify-tokens.mjs` to build BOTH artefacts, on the stated grounds that `exports["."]` now names `dist/plugin/index.js` and the fixture's `vite.config.ts` imports the package by name. `verify-frame.mjs` boots the SAME fixture — `const PROJECT = path.join(PKG, 'fixtures/consumer')` (line 46), and `fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts:17` does `import { designEditor, cssVariables } from '@wafflebase/design-editor'` — but `buildShellIfStale()` (lines 82-91) still runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts`, and `newestSourceMtime()` (line 106) still only stats `vite.shell.config.ts`, not `tsconfig.build.json`. On a clean checkout `boot()` therefore throws `dev server exited early: … Cannot find module`, reported as a broken fixture; on a dirty checkout every browser check runs against plugin bytes older than the change under test — the precise failure mode the diff's own comments call "worse than no gate".

samples.summary: A `&text=` subset face registered for a family can satisfy `document.fonts.check()/load()`, so the docs FontRegistry marks the family 'loaded' and the canvas / PDF export paints with the subset (missing glyphs)
samples.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` appends a stylesheet whose face, per this diff's own comments, "returns a face with no `unicode-range`" — i.e. it claims every codepoint for that family. `packages/docs/src/view/fonts.ts:302` short-circuits on `document.fonts.check(`12px ${JSON.stringify(family)}`)` and returns 'loaded' without loading anything or notifying re-layout listeners; line 309 awaits `document.fonts.load(fontSpec)`. Once a preview subset for e.g. "Open Sans" is loaded (the user merely scrolled the picker past that row), both calls can be satisfied by the subset, so `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:345-355` (`ensureFontLink` then `store.fonts.ensureFont`) can mark the family loaded and skip the re-layout notification while the real full face is still in flight — the applied document text then measures/paints with the label's glyphs only. `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pdf-actions.ts:32-40` has the same shape: `ensureFontLink` followed by `await document.fonts.load(`16px "${family}"`)` can resolve against the subset and the exporter snapshots pages before the full family arrives. Before this change every face present for a family was the full family, so a premature resolution was harmless.

samples.summary: Preview idempotency is per family, not per glyph set: a family previewed in the dropdown (label only) then shown in the More-fonts dialog renders the extra text (group name) in a fallback face
samples.evidence: `if (findPreviewFontLink(family)) return;` dedupes on family alone. The picker row's text is just the label (`font-family-picker.tsx:265-267`), while the dialog row's text is label + group name (`more-fonts-dialog.tsx:247-250`, both inside a button carrying `style={{fontFamily: entry.family}}`). So after scrolling a family past in the dropdown, opening "More fonts…" no-ops the second call and the group-name span paints with glyphs the earlier subset never requested — a visibly mixed row. The reverse order (dialog first, then dropdown) is safe only because the dialog's subset is a superset.

samples.summary: When the full-catalog load fails, `fullSettled` unblocks a `wght@400` preview for an out-of-catalog recent — the exact bad request the weight lookup exists to avoid, and the resulting broken link is permanent
samples.evidence: `const previewable = entry !== undefined || fullSettled;` becomes true via the `.finally()` at line 110-112 even on the `.catch()` path, so a recent from the 1,900-entry library with no known weights is previewed at the default first cut, `400`. For a single-cut family such as `Sunflower` the diff itself states `css2?family=Sunflower:wght@400` answers HTTP 400 with an HTML error page. Because `ensurePreviewFontLink` is idempotent on `findPreviewFontLink` (font-catalog.ts:267) and nothing ever removes the link, that row stays in a fallback face for the life of the page even after a later successful catalog load.

samples.summary: Opening the font dropdown now downloads the ~1,900-entry full-catalog chunk whenever any recent is outside the curated catalog, and re-attempts it on every open after a failed load
samples.evidence: `if (!moreOpen && !(open && needFullForRecents)) return;` fires `loadFullFontCatalog()` on a plain dropdown open, not only when the "More fonts…" dialog opens. `font-catalog-full-loader.ts:18-21` clears the memo on failure, and `fullCatalog` stays null, so with a flaky network every subsequent open re-requests the separate chunk. The saving being bought is a few hundred bytes of font subset per row.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: verify-frame.mjs boots fixtures/consumer (line 46), whose vite.config.ts:17 imports '@wafflebase/design-editor' by name; that self-reference resolves through package.json exports["."] to ./dist/plugin/index.js (package.json:9), and the fixture has no package.json of its own so the nearest boundary is the design-editor package. buildShellIfStale() (lines 82-91) runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts`, and vite.shell.config.ts:38-46 emits only dist/shell — nothing builds dist/plugin/index.js (that is `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`, package.json:20). newestSourceMtime() (95-107) also omits tsconfig.build.json, so an out-of-date plugin bundle is never rebuilt. dist/ is absent from the tree (gitignored per verify-tokens.mjs:143), so on a clean checkout boot() (118-144) throws 'dev server exited early: … Cannot find module'; on a dirty one every browser check runs against stale plugin bytes. I searched wide for a counterexample: the only invocation is package.json:23 'node ./scripts/verify-frame.mjs' with no pre-build wrapper anywhere in the repo (grep verify:frame/verify-frame), no committed dist, no alias or dependency remapping the package name to src, while all three sibling gates (verify-consumer.mjs:203-215, design-sandbox verify-scenes.mjs:95-105, verify-tokens.mjs:169-176) do build both artefacts and do stat tsconfig.build.json. Blocking under the correctness lens: a runtime crash on the script's real path plus a false-green stale-bytes path (broken invariant of the gate).

verdict.reason: The described code exists and at least one cited path is live. `ensurePreviewFontLink` (font-catalog.ts:258-284) registers a `&text=` subset face under the real family name, with no `unicode-range` per the module's own comment (font-catalog.ts:204); its guards (SSR/system/eager/`findPreviewFontLink`/`hasFullFamilyLink`, :263-271) only stop a subset when a full link ALREADY exists — they do not stop the preview-then-full ordering, and `ensureFontLink` (:152-164) never removes the subset link. On the export path, `pdf-actions.ts:31-39` appends the full link and then immediately awaits `document.fonts.load('16px "family"')`; the new stylesheet is still in flight, so a previously-loaded preview subset (created at font-family-picker.tsx:149 / more-fonts-dialog.tsx:151 by merely scrolling the picker) can satisfy the load and the exporter snapshots pages before the full family exists — `packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:122`'s `document.fonts.ready` also resolves immediately when nothing is actually loading, and nothing pre-links deck families on open. Partial weakness: the docs half of the narrative is currently inert — `FontRegistry` (docs/src/view/fonts.ts:278) is never instantiated outside tests and `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:351-354` reaches it through `store.fonts?.ensureFont?.()` on a DocStore with no `fonts` field, plus editor.ts:2663-2692 re-layouts on `loadingdone`/`fonts.ready`. That refutes only one of the two cited sinks, so the finding stands on the export path.

finding.summary: verify:consumer builds only the shell, never `dist/plugin` — the fixture consumer now resolves the plugin through `exports` to `dist/plugin/index.js`, so a clean checkout fails and a dirty one tests stale bytes
finding.evidence: The delta rewrites this docblock to claim "the build is its own `design-editor:build` lane besides, so a broken build fails before this script is reached". But no lane runs `verify:consumer` at all (grep: it exists only as a package script and in docs), so CI never guarantees anything for this script's inputs. `buildShellIfMissing()` (line 197-206) rebuilds ONLY `dist/shell/index.html` via `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts`; it never runs `build:plugin` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`). Since #966, `packages/design-editor/fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts:17` imports `@wafflebase/design-editor` BY NAME, and package.json:9 maps `.` to `./dist/plugin/index.js`. `dist/` is gitignored, so on a clean checkout `boot()` dies with `Cannot find module .../dist/plugin/index.js` — exactly the failure class the new `design-editor:build` lane was added to prevent elsewhere. Worse, when a stale `dist/plugin` exists, the staleness comparison at line 190-199 only compares src mtimes against the SHELL bundle, so an edit under `src/plugin/**` leaves the gate exercising the previously compiled plugin — the "gate that can pass on stale bytes" hazard the same comment warns about.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The finding claims a `buildShellIfMissing()` (lines 197-206) that rebuilds only the shell via `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` and never `build:plugin`. The actual function is `buildIfStale()` at verify-consumer.mjs:203-215, whose artefact list is `['dist/shell/index.html', 'dist/plugin/index.js']` (line 209) and which, when either is missing OR older than source, runs `pnpm run build` (line 213) — which package.json:21 defines as `build:shell && build:plugin`, emitting `dist/plugin/index.js` via `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` (package.json:20). So the claimed clean-checkout `Cannot find module .../dist/plugin/index.js` crash cannot occur: a missing `dist/plugin/index.js` is itself a build trigger at line 207. The second claim — staleness compared only against the shell bundle, so `src/plugin/**` edits go unnoticed — is also false: `newestSourceMtime()` (lines 166-181) walks all of `PKG/src` (including `src/plugin/**`) and additionally stats both `vite.shell.config.ts` and `tsconfig.build.json` (line 177), and that `newest` is compared per-artefact against `dist/plugin/index.js` too. Finally, the docblock the finding quotes ("the build is its own `design-editor:build` lane besides, so a broken build fails before this script is reached") does not exist; lines 187-196 state the opposite — "BOTH ARTEFACTS, not just the shell" and "NOTHING IN CI RUNS THIS SCRIPT ... `design-editor:build` therefore guarantees this script nothing". A repo-wide grep for `buildShellIfMissing` finds no source hits. The fixture premise is accurate (fixtures/consumer/vite.config.ts:17 imports the package by name, package.json:9 maps `.` to `./dist/plugin/index.js`), but that is precisely the hazard the present code already covers.

finding.summary: `pnpm design` rebuilds only when `src/shell` is newer than the shell bundle, so an edit under `src/plugin/**` silently runs against a stale compiled plugin (or a missing one is only caught by luck)
finding.evidence: `const shellStale = !existsSync(SHELL_DIST) || newestMtime(SHELL_SRC) > statSync(SHELL_DIST).mtimeMs;` with `SHELL_SRC = packages/design-editor/src/shell` (line 32) and `SHELL_DIST = dist/shell/index.html` (line 31). Since the exports map now names `dist/plugin/index.js`, `packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts` loads the COMPILED plugin, whose sources are `src/plugin/**`, `src/base.ts`, `src/tokens/adapter.ts`, `src/types.ts` (tsconfig.build.json:37) — none of which are in the staleness window. A developer editing the plugin then runs `pnpm design` and sees the old behaviour with no warning. Note the script starts the sandbox with `pnpm exec vite` (line 145-148), which bypasses design-sandbox's `predev: pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor build` safety net (packages/design-sandbox/package.json:10).

verdict.reason: The code described does not exist in this repository. `scripts/design.mjs` has no `shellStale`/`SHELL_SRC`/`SHELL_DIST` (repo-wide grep: no matches). Lines 39-43 define `EDITOR_DIST` as an array containing BOTH `dist/shell/index.html` AND `dist/plugin/index.js`, and `EDITOR_SRC` as the entire `packages/design-editor/src` tree — not `src/shell`. Line 140-141 computes `newestSrc = newestMtime(EDITOR_SRC)` and `distStale = EDITOR_DIST.some((f) => !existsSync(f) || newestSrc > statSync(f).mtimeMs)`, so an edit under `src/plugin/**`, `src/base.ts`, `src/tokens/adapter.ts` or `src/types.ts` does bump the staleness clock, and a missing `dist/plugin/index.js` is caught explicitly by `!existsSync(f)` rather than by luck. Lines 142-150 then run `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/design-editor build` (which emits both artefacts) before the server spawns at line 163, so the `pnpm exec vite` bypass of design-sandbox's `predev` (packages/design-sandbox/package.json:10) is compensated in-script. The exports map does name `./dist/plugin/index.js` (packages/design-editor/package.json:8-9), which is precisely the artefact the script now checks. The finding's premise — a staleness window narrowed to src/shell and one shell artefact — is absent.

finding.summary: verify:scenes builds the shell and core when stale but never the design-editor plugin dist its own vite.config now resolves
finding.evidence: `buildShellIfStale()` (line 66-86) runs only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts`, and `buildCoreIfStale()` (line 204-218) only `pnpm --filter @wafflebase/core build`; `main()` calls just those two (lines 222-223). `packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts` imports `@wafflebase/design-editor`, whose `exports["."]` is `./dist/plugin/index.js`. On a clean checkout the dev server it boots fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for the plugin entry rather than reporting a scene failure; with a stale dist it validates scenes against an out-of-date plugin. Same missing `build:plugin` step as verify-consumer.mjs / verify-frame.mjs.

verdict.reason: The code the finding describes is not in the named file. verify-scenes.mjs has no `buildShellIfStale()` (that name exists only in packages/design-editor/scripts/verify-frame.mjs:82). Instead verify-scenes.mjs:80-106 defines `buildDesignEditorIfStale()`, which folds `tsconfig.build.json` into the newest-mtime comparison (line 92), lists BOTH `dist/shell/index.html` and `dist/plugin/index.js` as artefacts to check for missing-or-stale (line 95), and on staleness spawns the package's own `pnpm run build` (line 102) — which package.json:21 defines as `build:shell && build:plugin`, i.e. it emits `dist/plugin/index.js` via `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` (package.json:20). `main()` awaits that before `boot()` (lines 241-243). So on a clean checkout the plugin entry that packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:49 imports IS built, and a stale dist is rebuilt by mtime rather than only-if-missing. The finding's cited line ranges (66-86, 204-218, 222-223), function name, and the claim that only `vite build --config ./vite.shell.config.ts` runs all fail to match the repository.

finding.summary: Preview subset link can shrink a family that the app shell already loaded in full (Inter / Fraunces / JetBrains Mono from index.html)
finding.evidence: `ensurePreviewFontLink` only refuses to inject a subset when (a) the catalog entry is `eager` (i.e. in `buildGoogleFontsHref`'s bootstrap link) or (b) a wafflebase-injected full link exists (`findFontLink`, line 226). It knows nothing about the *app-shell* stylesheet in `packages/frontend/index.html:12`, which loads `Fraunces`, `Inter` and `JetBrains Mono` in full. All three are curated-catalog entries with no `eager: true` (`font-catalog.data.ts:30`, `:64`, `:66`), so merely scrolling the font dropdown/dialog past the "Inter" row appends `css2?family=Inter:wght@400&text=Inter&display=swap` to `document.head` — declared *after* index.html's link, with no `unicode-range`, so by the author's own cascade reasoning (see the docstring at lines 206-210, which raises exactly this hazard for the full-link case) it wins font matching for weight 400 and the face then lacks every glyph outside "Inter". Inter is the app/token body font (`packages/core/scripts/build-css.ts:98` → `--font-body`) and the default Slides theme font (`packages/slides/src/themes/default-light.ts:20`), so the blast radius is app-wide UI text and Slides canvas text falling back to a system face for the rest of the session. The previous code path (`ensureFontLink`) requested the whole family and could not lose glyphs.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts ensurePreviewFontLink only checks the `eager` flag and wafflebase-injected links, and "knows nothing about the app-shell stylesheet in packages/frontend/index.html". The working tree contradicts this: font-catalog.ts:271 calls hasFullFamilyLink(family) before building any `&text=` subset link, and hasFullFamilyLink (font-catalog.ts:214-233) enumerates ALL `link[rel="stylesheet"]` elements in document.head — not marker-attributed ones — skipping its own preview links (:223) and other subset requests (:226), then whole-segment-matching each `family=` value with the axis spec stripped (:227-229) against both `%20` and `+` space spellings (:215-216). Applied to the actual shell href (packages/frontend/index.html:12), the segments resolve to `Fraunces`, `Inter`, `JetBrains+Mono`, all of which match, so the subset link is never appended for those three families. The function's docstring (:196-213) names this exact hazard. The finding's evidence is also mis-cited: it places findFontLink at line 226, but findFontLink is at :123-131 and 226 is inside hasFullFamilyLink — consistent with review of a stale revision. Regression tests pin the behavior: ensure-font-link.test.ts:211-245 installs the literal index.html href and asserts zero preview links for Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, and :254-256 asserts `Inter+Tight` does not falsely suppress `Inter`. The shell link is parser-inserted in <head> (index.html:10-13) before the deferred module script (index.html:48), so the guard is in place whenever ensurePreviewFontLink can run.
